video_metadata.title: My EXACT 4H Bias + BOS + FVG Setup (Short Setup Walkthrough)

input.transcript_snippet: Alright let me break down exactly how I find these setups. I start on the 4-hour chart. I need to know what the bias is. Today the 4H was bearish — price was trading below the 4-hour FVG that formed two days ago, so my bias is short. Once I have that bearish bias on the 4H, I drop to the 15-minute chart. I'm waiting for a bearish BOS or a CHoCH on the 15-minute. Once I see that break of structure to the downside, I know the 15-minute structure is now confirmed bearish aligning with my 4H bias. Now I come all the way down to the 5-minute chart. On the 5-minute I'm waiting for price to retrace back into an unmitigated bearish FVG. That's my entry trigger. The FVG has to be unmitigated — if price already came back to it once, I skip it. And I only take this during the NY AM session or the NY PM session, those killzones matter. I don't trade this at 2 PM randomly — it needs to be in a high-probability time window. Now I want to be clear — this works both ways. When the 4H is bullish, I'm looking for a bullish BOS on the 15-minute, then a bullish FVG retrace on the 5-minute, and I'm long. The logic is symmetric. I avoid FOMC and CPI days. My stop goes below the FVG plus some buffer. Average trade is about 2R when it works.

Enter on FVG close. SHORT: mirror — 4H bearish bias + 15m bearish BOS/CHoCH + price retraces into unmitigated bearish 5m FVG in killzone. Skip FOMC/CPI days.
strategies.bias_condition: 4H chart determines long/short bias — bearish when price trades below 4H FVG; bullish when price trades above
